>Enhance PowerVS subnet deletion logic to automatically handle attached network interfaces that block subnet removal (e.g., 409 Conflict).
>
>## Details
>
>- Add deleteNetworkInterfaces to enumerate and delete all NICs attached to a given subnet before retrying subnet deletion.
>- Introduce isNetworkInterfaceError helper to detect errors indicating subnet deletion is blocked by existing IP allocations or 409 conflicts.
>- Update deletePowerSubnet to:
>          - Detect NIC-related deletion failures
>          - Log the condition
>          - Attempt NIC cleanup
>          - Return a wrapped error to trigger the existing retry mechanism
>

>  * Improved DHCP network deletion reliability by proactively cleaning up attached network interfaces before retrying deletion.
>  * Enhanced detection and parsing of attachment errors to trigger automatic retries when deletions are blocked.
>* **Refactor**
>  * Streamlined network destroy workflow by deferring subnet handling to a later destruction stage, removing redundant wait/retry passes.
><!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

**Actionable comments posted: 2**
🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/destroy/powervs/power-dhcp.go (1)
`280-301`: **Minor: Potentially redundant network lookup on failure path.** If `findNetworkIDByName` was called successfully at line 267, `networkID` is already populated, so the condition at line 287 wouldn't trigger. However, if the initial lookup failed or was skipped (because `Network.Name` was nil), the second lookup at line 288 would also fail for the same reason. The current logic works correctly, but the second `findNetworkIDByName` call at line 288 is redundant in most scenarios.
♻️ Optional simplification ```diff if isDHCPNetworkAttachedError(err) { // Try to extract network ID from error message if we don't have it yet if networkID == "" { networkID = extractNetworkIDFromError(err) } - // If still no network ID, try finding by name again - if networkID == "" && dhcpServer.Network != nil && dhcpServer.Network.Name != nil { - networkID = o.findNetworkIDByName(*dhcpServer.Network.Name) - } + // Note: If networkID is still empty, finding by name was already attempted + // at lines 266-267 and failed, so no need to retry here. ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@pkg/destroy/powervs/power-dhcp.go` around lines 280 - 301, The code may call findNetworkIDByName redundantly when handling isDHCPNetworkAttachedError; simplify by ensuring networkID is retrieved once: if networkID is empty, attempt extractNetworkIDFromError(err) first, then if still empty and dhcpServer.Network != nil && dhcpServer.Network.Name != nil call findNetworkIDByName(*dhcpServer.Network.Name) to set networkID, then proceed to call deleteNetworkInterfaces(networkID) and return the wrapped error; remove the duplicate/secondary findNetworkIDByName lookup so networkID is only resolved once in the isDHCPNetworkAttachedError branch (references: findNetworkIDByName, extractNetworkIDFromError, isDHCPNetworkAttachedError, deleteNetworkInterfaces, networkID, dhcpServer, item.name). ```
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@pkg/destroy/powervs/power-dhcp.go`: - Around line 236-246: The substring match for "400" in isDHCPNetworkAttachedError is too broad and causes false positives; update the function (isDHCPNetworkAttachedError) to remove the raw "400" check or replace it with a more specific pattern such as "400 Bad Request" or another DHCP-specific marker (e.g., keep "pcloudDhcpDeleteBadRequest") so only DHCP-related 400 errors trigger true; ensure the function still checks the existing DHCP-specific strings ("still attached to pvm-instances", "still attached to", "pcloudDhcpDeleteBadRequest") but not a generic "400" substring. In `@pkg/destroy/powervs/power-subnet.go`: - Around line 74-83: The isNetworkInterfaceError function is matching the plain substring "409" which can produce false positives; update it to only detect HTTP 409 conflicts or the precise vendor message by removing the broad strings.Contains(errStr, "409") check and instead check for more specific markers such as "409 Conflict", "status 409", a word-boundary/regex match for "\b409\b", or (preferably) inspect a typed error/response to read an HTTP status code; modify isNetworkInterfaceError to use one of these tighter checks (or parse the error to extract a numeric status) while keeping the existing "one or more network interfaces have an IP allocation" sentinel check. --- Nitpick comments: In `@pkg/destroy/powervs/power-dhcp.go`: - Around line 280-301: The code may call findNetworkIDByName redundantly when handling isDHCPNetworkAttachedError; simplify by ensuring networkID is retrieved once: if networkID is empty, attempt extractNetworkIDFromError(err) first, then if still empty and dhcpServer.Network != nil && dhcpServer.Network.Name != nil call findNetworkIDByName(*dhcpServer.Network.Name) to set networkID, then proceed to call deleteNetworkInterfaces(networkID) and return the wrapped error; remove the duplicate/secondary findNetworkIDByName lookup so networkID is only resolved once in the isDHCPNetworkAttachedError branch (references: findNetworkIDByName, extractNetworkIDFromError, isDHCPNetworkAttachedError, deleteNetworkInterfaces, networkID, dhcpServer, item.name). ```
